newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended slightly firmer but well off their highs in heavy trading, knocked by a weak rand which reacted poorly to comments from central Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals.
However, some stocks, notably financial and banking shares, had yet another strong day with the financial index jumping to its fifth consecutive closing high, finishing at 8,431.
Gold stocks also held up well despite a struggling bullion price.
Dealers said trading had been choppy with initial weakness at the start of trade on the back of losses on Wall Street overnight erased early on.

But stocks were soon pushed weaker again when the rand lost over five cents against the dollar following comments from Stals that the currency's recent rally to six-and-a-half month highs could be a slight over-adjustment.
"The market looked positive at noon until Stals made a few comments which knocked five cents (off the rand) immediately," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
Marais said Stals' comment, made at the annual parliamentary briefing week in Cape Town, that the rand's appreciation may have been too quick weighed on the market.
Another dealer said: "After his talk the indices came down on a whole range of shares."

However, more upbeat was Stals' comment that interest rates may be cut towards the end of the year. He also said that the 1996 current account deficit would be well below the 1995 level of 10 billion rand.
Stock traders said futures players had been active in the market and volumes traded on Tuesday were heavy with around 963 million rands worth of shares changing hands.
Gold shares were stronger in early trade boosted by overnight New York demand for Dries spilling over into market.
Dealers said gold shares losses on bullion, which lost its grip on the $340 level, were cushioned by the weak rand which helped the index close positive.
Dealers said the market would continue firm on Wednesday as bullish undertones were still present.
"We are in positive territory but the market will keep an eye on Wall Street," Marais said.
The overall index gained 19.0 points to 6,975.0 points, industrials add 6.6 points to 8,293.1 and golds lift 7.9 points to 1,358.3 points.
Anglo was up 500 cents to 268 rand, SA Breweries put on 125 cents to 133.75 rand, Liberty Life dropped 50 cents to 130.00 rand and Stanbic shed 125 cents to 188.75 rand.
Dries made 125 cents to 43.75 rand, Kloof clipped 10 cents to 34.40 rand and Western Deep lost 150 cents to 146.50 rand.
Near-dated industrial index futures were weaker in late trade after see-sawing throughout the day. Gold contracts were steady and ignored on a dull bullion price.
Dealers said the industrial contracts weakened following Stals' speech and as long bonds and the rand fell. They were seen firm on Wednesday on continued bullishness in the market.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,455/65 from 6,443, the industrial contract was at 8,061/75 from 8,085 and the gold contract was at 956/62 from 947.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
